title: Renewal of C&I Contracts: New Pricing and Start of the New Term
content:
> Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts: renewals.

1. Every renewal is priced through a new pricing request with the request purpose renewal naming the contract, because every Beacon Ridge C&I structure requires new pricing for a renewal.
2. A renewal is signed only from a renewal pricing request whose pricing status is priced and only within its quote validity, counted as for a new contract.
3. A renewal signed while the contract is active starts the day after the contract end date; a renewal signed during holdover starts on the facility's next scheduled meter read date and returns the contract to active.
4. A renewal may change the structure and term; the new contract end date is counted from the term start date as at activation, that is, the day before the same calendar day the new term's number of months after the term start date.
5. A renewal never refunds or re-sizes a posted security deposit.

## Start of the new term (hypothetical dates)

| Status when the renewal is signed | Current contract end date | Scheduled meter reads | New term start date |
|---|---|---|---|
| active | 31 August 2026 | not relevant | 1 September 2026 |
| holdover, renewal signed 10 November 2026 | 31 August 2026 | 4 November and 3 December 2026 | 3 December 2026, the contract returning to active |

## New end date (hypothetical)

A 24-month renewal with a term start date of 1 September 2026: the same calendar day 24 months later is 1 September 2028, so the new contract end date is 31 August 2028.

## Points of judgement

- A renewal quote is checked exactly as a new quote is: pricing status priced, and signed within its quote validity.
- The security deposit already posted on the contract stays as it is when the renewal is signed.
